{"notes": "VISIT 1 (left at 1:00, very early, so ratings are provisional). I can't tell who placed which domino. I'm inferring only from hand positions and what people said.

Team: Fish plan agreed. All three accounts (Hana, Sofia, Jack) matched, and the picture fits it. The chain from the start is fully connected, with no visible breaks. It splits near x=6 into a long top-body branch and a short belly branch.

Hana: Drew the sketch and assigned strokes 1-5 clearly, and said the start and nose are down and connected. The picture supports that, since the start run is dark and joined. She said she'd check for breaks before the push. I'll look for her doing that on visit 2. She's the leadership/coordination candidate so far. Her roles were clear and consistent in both the private and public updates.

Sofia: Her hands were at the far end of the top-body line, about x=12, so that branch is well advanced and connected. She restated the plan aloud and checked in with Hana about the start and nose. That points to strong execution and decent collaboration. Watch whether the top line curves to meet the tail correctly.

Omar: His hands were at the end of the belly branch, which is short so far (about 2-3 units). It's connected, but he's behind Sofia. It's too early to judge, since he may have started later. Check pace next visit. Said nothing to me.

Jack: Tail strokes 4-5 are intentionally waiting on the body, so nothing is visible yet. He described the plan accurately and said he'd verify connectivity. Idle capacity: I'd like to see him help with the belly line or prep tail pieces rather than just wait.

No ratings yet. Follow up on: Omar's pace, Jack's use of waiting time, and whether Hana's break check actually happens."}
